headline: Housing and Consumer Rally Meets Oil and Iran Risk Ahead of Friday's Open
body_html:
Friday's session opens with investors weighing a lopsided Thursday against a Middle East backdrop that has not gone quiet. In the last completed session, 374 of the 533 stocks we track rose and 156 fell. Homebuilders gained 2.56% and consumer shares 2.55%, while semiconductors lost 1.28% and energy slipped 0.44%.

Overnight attention centers on diplomacy and crude. Qatari mediators are returning to Tehran to press for a US-Iran agreement, and President Trump said Vice President Vance's outreach to Iran concerns medical supplies. Oil is on course for a fourth straight monthly gain after a tanker attack near Hormuz underscored supply risk. Washington is also lending 40 million barrels from its strategic reserve, the last portion of a global arrangement.

At the open, watch whether Thursday's single-stock swings carry over. Glaukos jumped 33.65% and Crocs 25.54%, while Alnylam fell 25.13% and Fortinet 20.09%. Marvell (down 13.24%) and FormFactor (down 11.65%) will show whether the chip pullback deepens. Energy shares will take their cues from crude.

briefs.headline: Housing and consumer names set the pace
briefs.body: Homebuilders led Thursday's sectors with a 2.56% gain, with consumer shares just behind at 2.55%. Builders FirstSource climbed 12.85%, Crocs rose 25.54% and Boot Barn added 15.16%. The open will show whether buyers keep chasing these groups after such a sharp move.

briefs.headline: Healthcare split by two big single-stock moves
briefs.body: Healthcare gained 1.57% as a group, helped by Glaukos, which surged 33.65%. Alnylam went the other way, dropping 25.13% and ranking as the session's steepest decline among our top movers. Expect heavy attention on both names at the open.

briefs.headline: Software ends higher, but security stock stumbles
briefs.body: The software group rose 0.88% on Thursday, yet Fortinet sank 20.09%. Donnelley Financial bucked that weakness with a 14.97% advance. The split suggests investors are sorting winners from losers inside the sector rather than trading it as a single block.

briefs.headline: Chip stocks face a test after a rough session
briefs.body: Semiconductors were the weakest sector on Thursday, down 1.28%. Marvell Technology fell 13.24% and equipment maker FormFactor dropped 11.65%. Traders will look for signs of stabilization, or of further selling, when the market opens.

briefs.headline: Oil heads for a fourth monthly gain on supply worries
briefs.body: Crude is set to finish October with a fourth consecutive monthly advance, as an attack on a tanker near Hormuz keeps supply concerns alive. The US is lending 40 million barrels from its strategic reserve, the final share of a global agreement. Energy stocks slipped 0.44% Thursday.

briefs.headline: Investors split on Alphabet and Microsoft after earnings
briefs.body: Market commentators are debating why Alphabet is being punished after a difficult quarter while Microsoft escapes similar treatment. At least one analyst downgraded Alphabet and laid out where it would consider buying again. Reaction to the divergence could shape megacap trading at the open.
